<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard AUR package metadata and build instructions. There are no top-level commands, shell substitutions, or external data fetches that could execute malicious code during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The file defines variables (pkgname, pkgver, depends, source, sha256sums) and two standard functions (build() and package()) but does not contain any executable code at the top level that would run during the print-src-info phase. The source is specified as a GitHub archive URL (timg-$pkgver.tar.gz) which is the official repository. There are no suspicious patterns like eval, base64 decoding, curl/wget, or other dangerous command invocations. The checksum is present and not marked SKIP. Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe—it will simply read and parse the static PKGBUILD file without executing any untrusted or malicious code.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
